How we get to a good match.
If a wall needs rebuilding or a structural repair, bring in your mason or builder first. Once that work is finished, we can help with the color.

If your HOA has asked for a different color, we can help. We stain brick to match an approved sample or adjust its light reflectance value (LRV)—how much light it reflects. Send us the color or target you’ve been given. We’ll check the wall and any old coatings, test a sample, then stain the brick.
Instead of treating the wall as a new construction project, MCC worked with stain colors that visually canceled the unwanted siding pigment across the affected brick faces.

Learn how the color work is done

Look closely at an older wall and you’ll see several colors, not just one. We study those differences, mix and test colors against the brick and mortar, and check whether the surface can accept the treatment. The aim is a match that keeps the wall’s character, rather than covering it with one flat color.

MCC custom-mixes and applies color to installed brick, mortar, and other compatible materials. The work begins once a repair or addition is structurally complete and focuses on making the new material look at home beside the original.

We compare the treated area with the surrounding masonry up close and from a normal viewing distance. That wider view helps us judge how the lighter and darker tones work together, so the repair or addition reads as part of the wall rather than a separate patch.

We custom mix stains to work with the colors already in your wall, using small test samples to show how the color looks on your particular brick or mortar. We adjust the mix against the surrounding masonry or supplied standard before moving ahead with the work.

What should I send with an estimate request?

When paint on the siding starts to chalk, rain can wash that pigment onto the brick below. We use carefully matched stains to correct the discoloration and bring the brick closer to its original color. The source of the runoff needs attention too, so the problem doesn’t keep coming back.

When replacement brick doesn’t match, you don’t always need to replace it again. We can often adjust its color with stain. The same approach can help a new addition, mismatched mortar, or two brick deliveries that don’t quite match.
Will every masonry surface accept the same approach?
Yes. MCC welcomes residential and commercial inquiries for interior and exterior color work. Each review considers the installed material, existing finish, viewing distance, and surrounding color.
Your mason builds it. We match the color.

Your mason or builder finishes the construction first. If the new brick still stands out, we mix and test colors against the original wall, then adjust the new work to match its tones and natural variation.
